# Joseph and Aseneth Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS | **Section:** Aseneth Rises on the Eighth Day

---

**7:1** On the eighth day, before dawn and before the cock had crowed, Aseneth rose from her bed, for she had no more strength to weep.

**7:2** She said to herself: 'Where shall I turn? I have no one to whom I can flee for safety. All men hate me; my father Pentephres has pledged me to the firstborn son of Pharaoh; and Joseph hates me because I worshiped dead idols.'

**7:3** 'I will go to the God of my father and the God of Joseph, and I will call to him, for he is the Father of orphans and the Defender of the afflicted and the Helper of those who are oppressed.'

**7:4** Aseneth rose and went to the east window and looked toward the east. Behold, the sun was rising and the morning star was still shining in the sky.

**7:5** She said: 'Lord God of ages, who created all things and gave them the breath of life, who brought forth the invisible things into light and made all things and ordered them — to you I cry, Lord, as a little child who has no father or mother, and whom a stranger has taken prisoner.'

**7:6** 'My own father and mother have disowned me, because I destroyed and smashed their gods. I have no other hope but you, Lord, and no other refuge but your mercy, O Lord God.'

**7:7** Aseneth rose and removed the fine linen garments from the floor and put on a mourning robe — an old, worn black garment — and tied a sackcloth girdle around herself.

**7:8** She removed the golden crown from her head, the golden bracelets from her wrists, and the golden anklets from her feet, and threw them all on the floor.

**7:9** She poured ashes on her head, fell to the floor, beat her breast, and wept bitterly.

**7:10** She prayed to the Lord God of Joseph: 'Lord God of ages, who gives life and summons the living, who calls from darkness to light and from error to truth and from death to life — Lord, you alone are kind and compassionate and patient and most merciful and gentle, beyond all men and all gods.'

**7:11** 'To you, Lord, I flee for refuge; to you I bring my prayer; to you I cry out, Lord; and before you I confess my sins and the ungodliness of my fathers.'

**7:12** 'Have mercy on me, Lord, for I have sinned greatly before you. I am an impious woman who served dead and mute idols. Have mercy on me, Lord — I am desolate and afflicted.'

---
*SOPHIA: consensus rendering. Divergences logged in disagreement file.*
